reviews.title: No iPhone Duo support
reviews.text:
The app is stretched and letterboxed on iPhone Duo. Normally that would be expected with some leeway this close to the phone’s release but I’ve just seen on Anki’s forums the devs are saying they have no plans to support it and are instead focussing on ‘actual’ users. 

Extremely disappointing for an app that charges $40, especially when it’s free on literally every other platform except iOS. Do NOT buy this app if you own or plan to own an iPhone Duo.

reviews.title: The bare min, priced at the max
reviews.text:
You can review your cards. That's the best I can say about it.

Its business model is punitive, regressive, and spits in the face of the only people who support its existence, and its feature set and update schedule lag far behind what all other Anki users get for free... that part is genuinely a drag... but you *can* review your cards.

reviews.title: Abysmal, steep learning curve
reviews.text: If you want something simple, accessible, and user friendly, do not get this app. For the most basic language vocabulary you have to comb through tens of thousands of decks made by random people full of mistakes with thousands of cards. There is no simple “top 300 most common words” in a foreign language for example. And you have to leave the app, use a browser to comb through a junky insensible list, download a deck, and then it might not even import to the app correctly. Waste of money.

reviews.title: I thought people were exaggerating how bad the UI is
reviews.text:
The UI is about as intuitive as the first 5 minutes of learning Microsoft excel is. It just feels like an overwhelming and jumbled mess of features glued on a screen haphazardly.

If you think you can merely add cards then swipe through them you are wrong. It’ll take you quite some time to figure out how to do even that.

Normally this wouldn’t be upsetting, but for $25 a pop you’d think they could afford to bring on a UI designer and make this in *some way* intuitive. 

There are many features, but you’ll spend 90% of your study time trying to reverse-engineer this goofily unintuitive design to locate them. Wack.

reviews.title: The most frustrating app experience ever!
reviews.text:
I have spent over 40 minutes trying to figure out how to do a basic task—importing a CSV or TXT file—and NOTHING works. This is easily the most unintuitive app I have ever used.
The app references an "iTunes link," which is completely outdated and irrelevant for a mobile app in 2026. For an app that is extremely expensive compared to others in the category, the UI feels 15 years old and the workflow is a nightmare. There is no direct "import" button for cloud files; instead, you’re stuck in a loop of "invalid zip" errors and "EOCD" messages just trying to load a simple spreadsheet.
I bought this expecting a premium experience, but instead, I got a headache. Extremely frustrating. I want my money back.

reviews.title: The app technically works, but misses it’s objective

Eventually in a session, after seeing words 10 or 12 times, I can recognize the words. But the next day it is as if I have never seen them before. I am not retaining anything with this approach. My advice to others is to try to determine if a flash card approach is right for you before you buy this app.

reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.text:
I have used Anki on a computer, not bad.

But, on iPhone?

This ‘app’ is 

Awkward;
The UI is terrible; 
I cannot review cards I need to review-my deck is 2,000 words.

Why must I use a computer to build a new deck?

Why must I review 1,999 words to get back to the word I am learning as new?

I also use Algo App after importing from an Anki Deck, that app needs help, BUT their user experience has been user tested.

Anki has been a waste of time on iPhone.
